meta.title: Fliks: your personal video collection, on every screen
meta.description: Fliks is a self-hosted media server and streaming app for your own video collection. Free, open source, AGPL-3.0.

hero.title: Your personal video collection, on every screen in the house.
hero.subtitle: Point Fliks at the folders where your videos live and it does the rest: covers, descriptions, cast, seasons and episodes, laid out like the streaming apps you already use. Except the library is yours.
hero.note: Self-hosted. The server runs on your machine. No account to create, no subscription, nothing leaves the house.
hero.imageAlt: The Fliks home page, a library, discovery and a film page

features.title: What you get
features.subtitle: A full streaming service for the household, running on hardware you already own.

items.title: Adaptive streaming
items.text: Quality follows the bandwidth without a hiccup, or lock a bitrate by hand when you would rather decide.

items.title: Resume anywhere
items.text: Start on the phone, finish on the TV. The position syncs live.

items.title: Every track, switchable mid-playback
items.text: All embedded audio renditions, all embedded and external subtitles, with your choice remembered per show.

items.title: Subtitles found for you
items.text: A video with none? Fliks goes looking on the usual subtitle sites and picks the one that actually matches your copy.

items.title: Out of sync, fixed in one click
items.text: Fliks listens to the dialogue and slides the subtitles back onto it. No hunting for the right offset.

items.title: Translated on demand
items.text: Nothing available in your language? Translate a track you do have. The result is saved next to the video, so it is only done once.

items.title: Skip intro, next episode, chapter markers
items.text: Thumbnail previews when you scrub, and a rewind buffer for live TV.

items.title: Live TV
items.text: Add an M3U playlist or an Xtream account. Channels line up next to your library, with a program guide.

items.title: Several libraries side by side
items.text: Movies, shows, home videos, kids. Each pointed at its own folder.

items.title: Search across all of them
items.text: Filter and sort by status, date added, rating, runtime.

items.title: Rich metadata
items.text: Posters, fanart, genres, cast and crew. Every person and every genre is its own page.

items.title: Home rows
items.text: Continue Watching, Recently Added, and recommendations weighted by what you actually watched.

items.title: Spoiler protection
items.text: Blurs the synopsis, the thumbnail and the title of anything you have not watched yet, until you reveal it.

items.title: Recommend something to someone
items.text: Pick a film or a season and send it to another user. It shows up on their home page with your name on it.

items.title: Playlists
items.text: Your own running order, drag to reorder, autoplay from one item to the next.

items.title: Shared playlists
items.text: Invite other users as viewer, editor or admin and build one together.

items.title: Downloads that keep themselves current
items.text: What you have not watched is downloaded to the device, what you have watched is removed. Nothing to think about before a trip.

items.title: Multi-user
items.text: Each with their own history, progress and preferences.

items.title: Pairing by QR code
items.text: A short code or a scan, and the TV picks up the session from your phone.

items.title: Live transcode dashboard
items.text: For admins: who is watching what, at which quality, on which hardware path, and why.

items.title: Images cached locally
items.text: No hotlinking to external services while you browse.

plugins.title: Plugins
plugins.subtitle: Fliks ships with no way to acquire media. You install what you want from Settings > Plugins.

items.title: The Download plugin
items.text: Brings indexer search, download-client management and the grab pipeline. Install it and it appears in the interface.

items.title: Signed archives
items.text: Every plugin archive is signed, and the signature is checked before anything is written to disk.

items.title: Isolated by design
items.text: A data plugin ships JSON and executes nothing. A process plugin runs under its own uid, with its own database schema. It cannot reach another plugin's tables, or yours.

items.title: Part of the interface
items.text: Plugin pages, menu entries and settings appear where they belong, and follow your permissions like everything else.

platforms.title: Everywhere you watch
platforms.subtitle: Start a film on your phone and finish it on the TV. Your place follows you.
platforms.serverList: Docker, a Windows tray app, a macOS menu-bar app, or from source.

getStarted.subtitle: All you need is a folder with your videos.
getStarted.dockerStep2: Set your media path and passwords, then start it
getStarted.otherWays: Windows and macOS installers are on the releases page.

why.title: Why self-hosted
why.subtitle: The library is yours, and so is the machine it runs on.

items.title: Your data stays home
items.text: No account to create, no subscription, nothing leaves the house.

items.title: Free and open source
items.text: AGPL-3.0-or-later. Read the code, change it, run a modified version.

items.title: No catalog to lose
items.text: Your files, your metadata, your history. Nothing disappears because a license expired.

items.title: Runs on what you have
items.text: A NAS, a spare machine, a home server. Hardware transcoding when the machine offers it.

community.title: Open source, built in the open
community.subtitle: Every change, every release and every discussion happens on GitHub.

download.encodersSubtitle: Which hardware path is available depends on the machine, not on Fliks. It probes at startup and falls back to CPU when nothing else answers.
